authoring.question: q-125485
authoring.value: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $25{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$ oriented counterclockwise. Interpret circulation as the sum of four convergent improper line integrals over the open quadrant arcs, with independent one-sided limits at $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm5)$. The field is undefined at those four points, so the original ordinary circulation is not defined.
authoring.rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield 8pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.

decisions.reason: Retain the verified mathematical correction instead of reimporting the source error

authoring.question: q-125485
authoring.value:
The original field is undefined at the four axis intersections, so an ordinary line integral over the whole ellipse is not defined. For the explicit improper interpretation, $r(t)=(\cos t,5\sin t)$ traverses $25x^2+y^2=25$ counterclockwise. On each open quadrant arc,

$$\frac{5}{y}\,dx=\frac{5}{5\sin t}(-\sin t)\,dt=-dt,\qquad\frac{1}{x}\,dy=\frac{1}{\cos t}(5\cos t)\,dt=5dt.$$

Thus the scalar pullback is $4$. Each endpoint has the finite one-sided limit $4$, so each open-arc integral converges absolutely and equals $2\pi$. Their sum is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{imp}}=8\pi$, the unchanged option c. No principal-value cancellation is used, and $F$ remains undefined at the excluded points.
authoring.rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield 8pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.
